title: A Phone Call About Admitting a Costly Mistake at Work
script: Fitri: [thoughtful] Pak Hendra, I need to tell you something before you find out from the accounting report tomorrow morning.
Hendra: Go ahead, Fitri. Whatever it is, I would rather hear it directly from you.
Fitri: [carefully] I approved the wrong shipment quantity last week, and as a result, we ordered nearly three times more material than we actually needed.
Hendra: That's a significant amount, Fitri. Do you know yet how much this mistake is going to cost the company?
Fitri: [reflective] I calculated it this afternoon, and depending on how quickly we can return the extra material, it could be around fifteen million rupiah.
Hendra: I appreciate you telling me immediately instead of waiting to see if anyone would notice on their own.
Fitri: [honestly] I considered staying quiet for a moment, honestly, hoping the mistake might somehow go unnoticed, but I could not convince myself that was the right choice.
Hendra: If you had stayed silent and I discovered it later through the report, I would have questioned everything you approved after that as well.
Fitri: [seriously] I understand, and even though admitting this is embarrassing, I would rather you trust my honesty than doubt every decision I make from now on.
Hendra: Mistakes happen, Fitri, even to careful people. What worries me more than an error is someone who hides one out of fear.
Fitri: [gently] So what should we do now, given how much material we ordered by mistake?
Hendra: Contact the supplier first thing tomorrow and ask about their return policy, and I will speak with finance about adjusting this month's budget.
Fitri: [encouraging] Thank you for not immediately blaming me, even though this mistake is genuinely going to cost us both time and money.
Hendra: Everyone on this team will make mistakes eventually. What matters is whether they come forward, the way you just did.
Fitri: [sincere] I promise to double-check every shipment order from now on, no matter how routine it seems.
Hendra: Good. Now, let's fix this together instead of dwelling on what already happened.
